content:
- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is positive or neutral (e.g., +0.37 to +0.03); model tends to overshoot and fail to correct downward.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., -0.50 to -0.40), particularly in the first 10–15 days of the forecast horizon.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: overreacts to short-term volatility, then overcorrects, leading to prolonged overestimation in early forecast days.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag in price correction: model often misses downward trends that emerge after 10–12 days of negative sentiment.
- When sentiment is mixed or trending toward negative, reduce forecast slope; avoid steep upward revisions unless sentiment is strongly bullish.
- If sentiment is consistently negative over 3–5 days, reduce forecast by 5–10% from peak to avoid “overbought” mispricing.
- Avoid forecasting sharp upward moves after 2–3 consecutive days of negative sentiment — model tends to misread sentiment reversal.
